You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 65f8db8150ee30623cd6b870d6f836c4339026a5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2021 13:31:58 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/amdkfd: fix uint32 variable compared to less than zero

Currently the call to kfd_process_gpuidx_from_gpuid is returning an
int value and this is being assigned to a uint32_t variable gpuidx
and this is being checked for a negative error return which is always
going to be false. Fix this by making gpuidx an int32_t. This makes
gpuidx also type consistent with the use of gpuidx from the callers.

Addresses-Coverity: ("Unsigned compared against 0")
Fixes: cda0f85bfa5e ("drm/amdkfd: refine migration policy with xnack on")
Signed-off-by: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Reviewed-by: Felix Kuehling <Felix.Kuehling@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Felix Kuehling <Felix.Kuehling@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdkfd/kfd_svm.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdkfd/kfd_svm.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdkfd/kfd_svm.c
index cfd8065fe0f6..4cc2539bed5b 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdkfd/kfd_svm.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdkfd/kfd_svm.c
@@ -1330,7 +1330,7 @@ static void svm_range_unreserve_bos(struct svm_validate_context *ctx)
  */
 static int svm_range_validate_and_map(struct mm_struct *mm,
 				      struct svm_range *prange,
-				      uint32_t gpuidx, bool intr, bool wait)
+				      int32_t gpuidx, bool intr, bool wait)
 {
 	struct svm_validate_context ctx;
 	struct hmm_range *hmm_range;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect type assignment of the variable `gpuidx`, which was declared as `uint32_t` while it was being assigned the return value of a function that returns an `int`. This led to a situation where negative error values from the function could not be properly checked, as the unsigned type would always evaluate to false when compared to zero. The fix involved changing the type of `gpuidx` to `int32_t` to ensure proper handling of negative values and maintain type consistency with its usage in the code.
